Refer to the infographic on mid-latitude cyclones. The mid-latitude cyclone mentioned in the extract is in the (initial/mature) stage.
Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 1.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: A well-developed cold front (2); Widespread rainfall to the Western Cape/affects the south-western Cape/made landfall (2); Well-developed cold sector and warm sector (2); Presence of the cumulonimbus cloud ahead of the cold front (2); Steep gradient (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why did the rainfall mentioned in the extract spread from Cape Town to Mossel Bay and Knysna?
subQuestions.memoText: Driven/steered by the westerly winds (2); The mid-latitude cyclones move from west to east (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the graph and determine the lowest and highest rainfall, in millimetres, recorded in the Western Cape over 36 hours.
With reference to the cross-section, explain how a well-developed cold front results in heavy rainfall over the Western Cape.
subQuestions.memoText: Cold front (cold air) undercuts warm moist air (2); Resulting in rapid uplift of warm moist air (2); Rising air cools and condenses (2); (Extensive/great vertical extent) cumulonimbus clouds develop (2). [ANY TWO – PROCESSES] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: How will the heavy rainfall negatively affect the physical (natural) environment in and around the Western Cape?
subQuestions.memoText: Will result in soil erosion (accept examples) (2); Biodiversity will be destroyed (2); Destruction of natural habitat (accept examples) (2); Destruction of natural vegetation (2); Loss of wildlife (2); Destruction of food chains/ecosystems/food webs (2); Will cause mass movements (accept examples) (2); Fertilisers washed into the rivers (causing eutrophication) (2); Will result in water pollution (accept examples) (2); Leaching of soil nutrients (2); (Low-lying) areas are flooded (2); Waterlogged conditions (saturation of soil) (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the satellite image of a tropical cyclone in the mature stage. State ONE condition required for the development of the tropical cyclone.
subQuestions.memoText: Presence of Coriolis force (1); Ocean surface temperature of at least 26,5 °C (1); Calm (surface) conditions for several days/less friction (1); Presence of low (air) pressure (1); Unstable atmospheric conditions (1); Evaporation from the sea surface/rising of warm moist air (1); Upper air divergence (1); Latent heat (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: In which hemisphere did this cyclone develop?
Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 1.4.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Air circulation around the low-pressure cell is clockwise (2); Forward (leading) left-hand quadrant/dangerous semi-circle is located on the south-west of the tropical cyclone (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to A and B on the satellite image. Differentiate between the cloud cover at A and B.
subQuestions.memoText: A – has clear skies (1); B – dense (cumulonimbus) cloud cover (1). (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why there is a difference in the cloud cover at A and B.
subQuestions.memoText: At A (eye) – air is descending (heating), resulting in no condensation (no formation of clouds) (2); At B (eye wall) – air is rising (cooling), resulting in condensation (the formation of clouds) (2). (2 x 2). [PART MARKING – MAXIMUM OF TWO: At A (eye) air is descending (1); At B (eye wall) air is rising (1)]

subQuestions.questionText: Why are the strongest winds found in the forward (leading) left-hand quadrant?
subQuestions.memoText: Combination of the forward movement and rotation of the system (2); It has a steep pressure gradient (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Draw a sketch of a tropical cyclone in its mature stage as represented on a synoptic weather map. Indicate the following on the sketch:
(i) Air pressure reading at the centre of the tropical cyclone
(ii) At least four isobars indicating the correct spacing
(iii) Symbol to represent the tropical cyclone
subQuestions.memoText: (i) Pressure reading at centre of eye must not be more than 996 (range 950–996) (1); (ii) 4 isobars indicating the correct spacing (1); (iii) Correct symbol showing the Southern Hemisphere (clockwise rotation) (1). (3 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketches on berg winds. Name the high-pressure cell and low-pressure cell indicated on the sketch map that leads to the development of berg winds.
Which sketch (A or B) represents the formation of berg winds?
Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 1.5.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Air from the interior (KHPC) descends down the escarpment (2); The air from the KHPC moves towards the low pressure (2); Air is offshore towards the ocean (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why cloudless conditions are indicated by the station model at X on the sketch map.
subQuestions.memoText: Air descending the escarpment (is offshore) hence dry (2); Descending air heats up resulting in no condensation (no formation of clouds) (2); Descending air heats up and the remaining moisture is evaporated (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2). [PART MARKING: Descending air (heats up) (1)]

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain how berg winds impact negatively on the natural vegetation and suggest strategies that can be put in place to limit this negative impact.
subQuestions.memoText: IMPACT: A berg wind dries out the natural vegetation (2); Berg winds increase the temperature of the area and make it vulnerable to veld fires (2); The veld fires destroy the natural vegetation (2). STRATEGIES: Create firebreaks (2); Ensure water accessibility (accept examples) (2); Awareness of the negative impact of veld fires (2); Availability of emergency services (2); Build/maintain/monitor lookout towers/warning systems (accept examples) (2); Education of the community (2); Developing of wind breaks (2). [ANY FOUR – MUST INCLUDE BOTH IMPACT AND STRATEGIES] (4 x 2)

(i) interlocking spurs.
(ii) a valley within a valley.
(iii) paired terraces.
(iv) incised meanders.

A (i) and (iii)
B (i) and (iv)
C (ii) and (iii)
D (ii) and (iv)

Refer to the sketch showing river rejuvenation. The longitudinal profile of the river after river rejuvenation would be …

A Profile A
B Profile B
C Profile C
D Profile D
Refer to the drainage patterns illustrated in sketches A and B. Identify the drainage patterns in sketches A and B.
State the underlying rock structure and rock type on which the drainage pattern in A developed.
subQuestions.memoText: Rock structure: Jointed/faults (1) OR Horizontally layered (1) [ANY ONE]. Rock type: Igneous (1) OR Sedimentary (1) [ANY ONE]. (1 + 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the underlying rock structure influenced the drainage pattern in A.
subQuestions.memoText: Rivers flow in joints that have 90° bends (2); Tributaries join main streams at 90° angles (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: The drainage density in B is (high/low).
Determine the stream order at X.
Explain the relationship between stream order and drainage density in B.
subQuestions.memoText: The higher the stream order, the higher the drainage density (2). (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the slope (gradient) and permeability of underlying rock influence the drainage density in B.
subQuestions.memoText: The steeper slope (gradient) promotes run-off (cuts more river channels) (2); Rocks with low permeability (impermeable) promote more run-off (less infiltration) (2). (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketches on river capture (stream piracy). Which river (A or B) has more erosive power?
Give ONE reason evident in the sketches to support your answer to QUESTION 2.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText: It is flowing at a lower level (220 m) (2); It has captured river B (2); River A erodes (headward) through the watershed (2); Steeper gradient to the watershed (220–880 m) (2); More volume of water at River A (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify features C and D.
subQuestions.memoText: C – Elbow of capture (1); D – Wind gap (1). (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE characteristic of feature D.
subQuestions.memoText: It is a dry area (2); It has river gravels (2); It is located below the elbow of capture (2); It is located above the misfit stream (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, describe the changes that river E will experience after river capture has taken place.
subQuestions.memoText: Volume of water of the river decreases (2); River's velocity/speed decreases (2); River has less energy (2); River has less erosive ability (2); River will experience more deposition (2); The length of the river is shortened (2); Stream order will decrease (2); River will become non-perennial (accept episodic/periodic) (2); Width of the river is reduced (2); Size of the drainage basin decreases (2). [ANY FOUR] (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the extract on catchment and river management. How much water is lost due to alien plants, according to the extract?
subQuestions.memoText: (More than) 100 million litres (1); 20% of daily use (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO plans in the extract that the Cape Town municipality intends to use to improve water security.
subQuestions.memoText: Extract ground water (drilling boreholes) from aquifers (1); Alien clearing programmes (1); Catchment restoration and maintenance (1). [ANY TWO] (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, what are the challenges that are faced when implementing these plans (answer to QUESTION 2.5.2)?
subQuestions.memoText: Less availability of ground water due to alien plants (2); Underfunding (2); Inefficiencies (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the positive impact of the removal of alien plants on the:
(a) Volume of water in the dam
subQuestions.memoText: It will increase the volume of water in the dam (2). (1 x 2)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the positive impact of the removal of alien plants on the:
(b) Water table
subQuestions.memoText: The water table will be higher (2). (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why will the removal of alien plants improve the biodiversity of the catchment area?
subQuestions.memoText: There will be more water for the plants (2); More water available for animal species (2); More water will increase aquatic habitats (2); More water will improve food supply for animal species (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2)

Calculate the area in m² of the farm labelled F in block E3 on the topographical map. Use the following measurements: the length on the map is 0,9 cm and the breadth on the map is 0,7 cm.

Formula: Length x Breadth
subQuestions.memoText: Formula: Length x Breadth. (0,9 cm x 500 m) x (0,7 cm x 500 m) [Given] = 450 m (1) x 350 m (1) = 157 500 m² (1). (3 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the average gradient from 6 in block D4 to 7 in spot height 1567 in block D2 if the horizontal equivalent (HE) is 950 m on the orthophoto map.

Formula: Vertical Interval (VI) ÷ Horizontal Equivalent (HE)
There is no intervisibility between 8 in block D4 and 9 in block D2 on the orthophoto map. Name the type of slope responsible for this.

Map evidence indicates … rainfall because of the … blue lines on the topographical map.
(i) annual
(ii) seasonal
(iii) continuous
(iv) dashed

A (i) and (iii)
B (i) and (iv)
C (ii) and (iii)
D (ii) and (iv)
Refer to the encircled area G in block B1 on the topographical map. Explain how the katabatic wind influences the temperatures at G in block B1 on the topographical map.
subQuestions.memoText: Cold wind drains down the valley slopes and accumulates at the valley floor, decreasing the temperature (2). (1 x 2). [PART MARKING – MAXIMUM OF ONE: Cold wind drains down the valley slopes (1)]

subQuestions.questionText: The table below shows crops and the temperatures at which these crops are likely to survive: Pumpkin −2 °C; Tomatoes 5 °C. Which crop (pumpkin or tomatoes) is most likely found at G in block B1 on the topographical map?
Give a climatological reason for your choice (answer to QUESTION 3.2.3).
subQuestions.memoText: Frost pockets are found at the bottom of the valley (valley floor/G) (2); Area where the temperatures are below freezing point/G (2); Pumpkin can withstand temperatures below freezing point (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the river at 10 on the orthophoto map. The river at 10 on the orthophoto map generally flows in a (south-westerly/north-easterly) direction.
Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 3.2.5.
subQuestions.memoText: The highest point is to the north-east/spot height 1524 (2); The V-shaped contour lines point to areas of increasing heights to the north/north-east (2); The acute angles formed by the tributaries joining the main stream point in a south-westerly direction (2); Dam wall on the southern side (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the river at H on the topographical map. In which stage (upper course/middle course) is the river at H in block B5 on the topographical map?
subQuestions.memoText: Upper course (B5/H: upper) (1). [Accept C3: middle. ANY ONE – LINKED TO 3.2.8] (1 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the topographical map to support your answer to QUESTION 3.2.7.
subQuestions.memoText: Upper course: Near the source (2); Contours closely spaced (2); Steep gradient (2); V-shaped valleys (2). Middle course: U-shaped valley (2); Contours far apart (2); Gentle gradient (2); River meanders (2). [ANY ONE – LINKED TO 3.2.7] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText:
The environmental issue labelled I in block A2 is represented as a … feature on the topographical map.

A point
B polygon
C node
D line
Remote sensing is defined as taking images of the Earth's surfaces from a distance. Explain how remote sensing can be used to effectively monitor the environmental issue mentioned in QUESTION 3.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: To determine if the environmental issue is getting worse (accept examples) (2); Images can be updated/monitored regularly (2); Images can be analysed (2); Determine possible causes (2); Provide possible solutions (2). [ANY ONE – PROCESSES] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: The municipality provides a GIS specialist with the topographical map and orthophoto map to check the availability of water at dam J (topographical map) and 11 (orthophoto map). Define the concept raster data.
subQuestions.memoText: A representation of geographical features using pixels/grid cells (2). [CONCEPT] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: A (topographical map/orthophoto map) is a representation of raster data.
Why is the information on the orthophoto map more realistic when determining the availability of water in the dam at a specific time?
subQuestions.memoText: It is an image which shows the real dam and the water it contains (2); Tone reflects the depth (2); Texture indicates whether there is water in the dam (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)
